findings.claim: The lesson presents a different set of twelve user groups as the specification list.
findings.truth: The specification's twelve categories include people from different ethnic groups, people with family commitments, parents (single or coupled), people who work, and one combined unemployment/economic-disadvantage category. The lesson substitutes or splits several of these. Correcting it would require coordinated changes to headings, content, conclusion, questions and flashcards; revise the whole user-group list together.
findings.evidence: OCR Cambridge Nationals in Sport Studies J829, Unit R184, 1.1.1 (local specification).

findings.claim: The Olympic Creed is attributed to Bishop Ethelbert Talbot rather than Pierre de Coubertin.
findings.truth: The course specification presents the Creed with Pierre de Coubertin as speaker, while Olympic historical material describes an earlier Talbot connection before Coubertin's adoption of the phrase. Keep a historically qualified attribution, or align the learner-facing version to the course specification; the source conflict makes a one-line correction unsuitable.
findings.evidence: OCR J829 R184, 2.2.1 (local specification); Olympic World Library history of the Olympic Creed (fetched).

findings.claim: The nine participation barriers omit the positive family-role-model/family-support barrier and change several specified labels.
findings.truth: Use the nine R184 barriers, including positive sporting role models, positive family role models/family support, appropriate activity provision, awareness of appropriate provision, and equal media coverage in terms of gender and ethnicity.
findings.evidence: OCR Cambridge Nationals in Sport Studies J829, Unit R184, 1.2.1 (local specification).

findings.claim: Football is said to have over 11 million registered adult participants in England.
findings.truth: The FA's 11-million figure was for total participants, not registered adults; Sport England's Active Lives reporting gives nearly four million adult football participants.
findings.evidence: The FA, The Football Association Annual Report 2015 (fetched); Sport England, Active Lives (fetched).

findings.claim: Padel England is described as the recognised NGB and UK court numbers are stated as above 1,000 by 2025.
findings.truth: The LTA became Britain's padel NGB in 2020. Its 2024 strategy reported 350 courts and a target of 1,000 by the end of 2026, not a verified 2025 total above 1,000.
findings.evidence: LTA, 'LTA confirms it is now the National Governing Body for Padel in Britain' (13 Nov 2020) and LTA Padel Strategy 2024 (fetched).

findings.claim: Dina Asher-Smith is described as preparing for the Paris 2024 100m final.
findings.truth: Asher-Smith competed in the 100m semi-final at Paris 2024 but did not progress to the final.

findings.claim: Paris 2024's Olympic Village is said to have housed over 14,500 athletes from 206 nations.
findings.truth: Paris 2024 had 10,500 Olympic athletes from 206 delegations; the 14,500 accommodation figure includes athletes and staff.
findings.evidence: Paris 2024 official athlete/delegation facts and Paris 2024 Olympic legacy reporting (fetched).

findings.claim: 'Inspiring a Generation' is described as UK Sport's 2012 legacy programme funding grassroots sport for a decade.
findings.truth: 'Inspiring a Generation' was a British Wheelchair Basketball participation programme supported by Sport England and National Lottery funding, not a UK Sport 2012 legacy programme.
findings.evidence: UK Sport, British Wheelchair Basketball 'Inspiring a Generation' programme article (2021, fetched).

findings.claim: The Taylor Report's all-seater recommendation is limited to 'top-flight' grounds.
findings.truth: The all-seater requirement applied to clubs in the top two divisions, with the August 1994 deadline.
findings.evidence: UK Parliament Hansard, football all-seater requirement discussion (fetched).

findings.claim: The WADA summary says the List has nine categories and says alcohol remains prohibited in particular sports.
findings.truth: The List has ten substance categories (S0–S9) and three method categories (M1–M3). Alcohol was removed from the List in 2018; beta-blockers remain prohibited in particular sports.
findings.evidence: WADA 2026 Prohibited List and WADA notice on removal of alcohol from the 2018 List (fetched).

findings.claim: Russian athletes' Paris 2024 AIN designation is attributed to ongoing doping sanctions and a non-existent body is named.
findings.truth: Eligible Russian and Belarusian athletes competed as Individual Neutral Athletes under Paris 2024 eligibility conditions linked to Russia's war in Ukraine. World Athletics had reinstated RusAF from its doping suspension in 2023 but continued the separate Russia/Belarus exclusion.
findings.evidence: IOC Paris 2024 Individual Neutral Athlete eligibility information and World Athletics announcement on RusAF reinstatement/exclusion (fetched).

findings.claim: Paris 2024's organising budget and public spending are framed as an 8.8bn-euro cost overrun and taxpayer gap.
findings.truth: The Paris 2024 Organising Committee's final budget was about €4.48bn. The French Court of Auditors estimated public spending connected to the Games at €6.6bn; these are different measures, not evidence of the stated budget overrun.
findings.evidence: Paris 2024 Organising Committee final financial reporting and Cour des comptes Paris 2024 report (fetched).

findings.claim: Athens 2004 is assigned a pound-denominated 7–9bn cost and presented as a direct cause of later inability to maintain venues.
findings.truth: Reliable accounts give differing euro-denominated cost estimates and document many underused venues, but do not establish the lesson's simplified currency figure or a direct causal account of Greece's fiscal crisis. Use a single sourced euro figure and present the causal relationship as contested, or omit the figure.
findings.evidence: Athens Social Atlas Olympic cost analysis and Kathimerini reporting on Athens 2004 venues (fetched).

findings.claim: The lesson says four particular NGBs are the ones students must name.
findings.truth: R184 requires named, current NGB examples but does not prescribe those four bodies.
findings.evidence: OCR Cambridge Nationals in Sport Studies J829, Unit R184, 4.1 (local specification).

findings.claim: Rugby impact sensors are described as being in helmets.
findings.truth: World Rugby's head-impact system uses instrumented mouthguards, which can measure head acceleration and flag a possible concussion for medical assessment.
findings.evidence: World Rugby, Head Impact Measurement and Care (fetched).

findings.claim: Doping sanctions are presented as a universal warning-to-fine-to-ban-to-prosecution ladder.
findings.truth: Sanctions depend on the anti-doping rule violation, substance or method, fault and prior violations; a first intentional violation can result in four years' ineligibility. Criminal proceedings for trafficking depend on national law.
findings.evidence: WADA Code, Article 10, and UK Anti-Doping sanctions guidance (fetched).

summary: Checked all 10 lessons against OCR J829 R184 and fetched primary/official sources. Logged 16 findings: 13 FIX and 3 ADJUDICATE. The 30 edits are exact, surgical corrections; quotation attribution, the unit-wide user-group list and the contested Athens legacy claim are deliberately left without edits.
